fig01_campaign_overview: Overview of the BACSAM-II campaign region. Grey lines show the flight tracks of all Polar 6 research flights. The coloured lines highlight the flight paths of the four low-level flights of which data are used in this study. The coloured rectangles (dashed lines) outline the corresponding focus regions shown in Fig. 4a–d. The background shows the mean sea-ice concentration for April 2024 from the merged MODIS–AMSR2 product (Ludwig et al., 2020). The black star marks the operating base Longyearbyen.
fig02_meteo_overview: Thermodynamic lower-boundary conditions for the bulk flux estimates. **(a)** Profiles of potential temperature on the four BACSAM-II low-level flight days, constructed from $\theta_\mathrm{s}$ at the surface and the potential temperature at the T-Bird and Polar 6 flight heights (observations) or at the model and height levels of the reanalyses. Thin lines show individual segments and thick lines the median profile. Dashed horizontal lines indicate the mean flight heights above the surface. Colours distinguish the observations, ERA5–MODIS, ERA5, and CARRA. **(b)** Normalized distributions of $T_\mathrm{s}$, with surface-regime ranges indicated by the shaded background. **(c)** Normalized distributions of the near-surface potential temperature difference $\Delta\theta=\theta_\mathrm{air}-\theta_{\mathrm{s}}$ (Eq. 3).
fig03_leg_length: Sensitivity of the EC sensible heat flux to the length of the averaging sub-window for the six T-Bird low-level legs during BACSAM-II (median leg length 70.2 km). **(a)** Mean EC flux of the sub-windows relative to the EC flux of the stretch they cover ($H_\mathrm{S,sub}/H_\mathrm{S,cov}$), averaged over five positions of the window grid (mean and standard deviation over the legs with a flux of at least $0.5$ W m$^{-2}$). **(b)** Random error $\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$ of the sub-window fluxes (median and quartiles; Appendix A). **(c)** Fraction of sub-windows whose flux magnitude exceeds $1$, $2$, and $3\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$. The dashed vertical line marks the 5 km window used in this study.
fig04_flux_maps: EC fluxes of the 5 km low-level segments flown during BACSAM-II (April 2024). Red/blue colour shading indicates the EC sensible heat flux, white/blue colour shading the sea-ice concentration, and wind barbs denote the mean wind speed and direction. The frame colours correspond to the focus-region rectangles in Fig. 1. **(a)** 13 April 2024, northernmost flight leg over consolidated pack ice. **(b)** 15 April 2024, compact sea ice with leads east of Svalbard. **(c)** 17 April 2024, overflight of the opening Whalers Bay polynya north of Svalbard over mostly thin sea ice. **(d)** 23 April 2024, same area as in (c), with the polynya now exposing open water.
fig05_flux_timeseries: **(a)–(f)** Along-track SHF time series of the six low-level flight legs during BACSAM-II from the T-Bird bulk, ERA5–MODIS bulk, and ERA5-only bulk estimates, the ERA5 and CARRA model-diagnosed fluxes, and the EC reference (Table 1). The dotted grey line marks zero SHF. Positive values denote upward turbulent heat flux from the surface to the atmosphere. **(g)–(l)** MODIS/Terra ice-surface temperature (IST) imagery of the same day (NASA Global Imagery Browse Services) with the analysed flight legs. White areas indicate missing values (cloud-obscured pixels). **(m)–(r)** MODIS/Terra true-colour imagery of the same scenes, with the flight legs coloured by $H_\mathrm{S,obs,EC}$.
fig06_flux_scatter: Comparison of the bulk and model-diagnosed sensible heat flux estimates with the EC reference over the 91 segments. **(a)** Scatter comparison of the T-Bird bulk flux $H_\mathrm{S,obs,bulk}$ with the EC flux $H_\mathrm{S,obs,EC}$, colour-shaded by the in situ bulk Richardson number $Ri_\mathrm{b}$ of the T-Bird bulk estimate (colour scale saturating beyond $\pm0.5$). The dashed line shows the ordinary least-squares fit of the estimate on the reference, the grey line the 1:1 relation, and grey bars the 1$\sigma$ uncertainty of each estimate. **(b)** Histograms of $H_\mathrm{S,obs,EC}$, $H_\mathrm{S,obs,bulk}$, and $H_\mathrm{S,RS,bulk}$. Continuous lines show the smoothed kernel-density estimate. **(c)** As (a), for $H_\mathrm{S,RS,bulk}$, with the colours again showing the in situ $Ri_\mathrm{b}$. **(d)** As (b), for the reanalysis-based estimates $H_\mathrm{S,ERA,bulk}$, $H_\mathrm{S,ERA,diag}$, and $H_\mathrm{S,CAR,diag}$ ($n = 74$), with the EC reference in black.
fig07_sensitivity: Skill of representative bulk configurations against the EC reference for $H_\mathrm{S,obs,bulk}$ (green), $H_\mathrm{S,RS,bulk}$ (orange), and $H_\mathrm{S,ERA,bulk}$ (blue). **(a)** Amplitude skill, given by the regression slope $b$ on the EC flux. **(b)** Variability skill, given by the Pearson correlation $r$. **(c)** Bias. The grey dashed lines in (a) and (c) mark the ideal values. The model-diagnosed fluxes $H_\mathrm{S,ERA,diag}$ and $H_\mathrm{S,CAR,diag}$ $^{*}$ (bottom rows) do not depend on the bulk configuration. The first row is the reference configuration (GLGS20, conventional $\alpha_T = 10^{-1}$, surface-type-dependent roughness). Every other row changes one setting at a time. Only representative members of each experiment are shown. Table C1 lists the slopes and Pearson correlations of the T-Bird and ERA5–MODIS bulk estimates for every tested configuration. $^{*}$CARRA is unavailable on 13 April and is evaluated on $74$ instead of $91$ segments.
figA1_spectral_qc: Spectral diagnostics of the $91$ T-Bird segments. Blue lines mark segments whose SHF exceeds $2\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$, grey lines the segments below $2\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$, and the black line is the median. **(a–d)** One-sided power spectra of potential temperature, vertical wind speed, and the horizontal wind components. Grey shading marks the 0.1–20 Hz frequency interval used for the EC SHF estimate. Diagonal dashed lines show reference slopes proportional to $f^{-5/3}$. **(e)** Frequency-weighted $w$–$\theta$ cospectra. **(f)** Normalized $w$–$\theta$ ogives, the cumulative covariance from high to low frequencies, for the SHF values above $2\,\sigma_\mathrm{rand}$. The spectra in (a)–(e) are Welch estimates with 8 s windows and therefore start at 0.125 Hz, whereas the ogives in (f) are computed from the full segment.
